state.assignment_rule: A tier is dropped for a class when any measured dimension fails inside it. Survivors rank by total burden: surface, packaging, and per-call cost. Catalogue wins ties only for generic cross-app surfaces. Companion needs shown auth and release parity. A class with no fully evidenced tier goes back to preparation instead of receiving an assumed tier.
state.class_chart: Widget C renders an invoice-totals bar chart, selects one bar, and disposes. Adapter prototype: 3 synchronous operations, 3 failure leaves, 1 callback governed by 4 dispatch rules (single dispatch, sealed reporting, immediate reentrant update, dispose during callback), deep immutable copies at each crossing, opaque tokens, idempotent dispose, 279 lines, 6051-byte bundle excluding real SDK bytes. Companion prototype: render, select, and release over typed envelopes, 7 failure leaves, zero callbacks, frozen bytes plus table per render, idempotent release, select after release expires, 209-byte render request and 164-byte response pinned, 360 lines, 20236-byte bundle including 11041 shared policy bytes. Both tiers satisfy the workflow; the adapter keeps selection local while the companion keeps SDK bytes out of the audited browser asset. Catalogue sketch: minimal vendor-neutral chart operations with a per-release fixed renderer, selectable only if charts become platform surface; building from existing operations is excluded by missing canvas and SVG primitives.
state.class_clipboard: Op B exchanges text with the device clipboard through an async permission-gated platform API. Adapter prototype: 2 async operations, 4 failure leaves, permission pre-gate with fail-closed denial, explicit no-ordering rule for concurrent calls, zero callbacks, 156 lines, 2987-byte bundle. Companion prototype: a server pastebin cell over typed envelopes, 9 failure leaves, pinned 106-byte read and 127-byte write requests, 301 lines, 16768-byte bundle including shared policy bytes. Measured gap: the server cell and the device cell stay disjoint, so the companion cannot serve the device-clipboard workflow and fails the compare-targets dimension. Catalogue sketch: 2 generic operations with 4 errors, selectable after live permission-matrix qualification plus a second app need.
state.class_storage: Op A persists string keys and values through a synchronous platform store with quota and origin gating. Adapter prototype: 3 synchronous operations, 3 failure leaves, zero callbacks, zero copy crossings, availability gate with no host contact, 184 lines, 4559-byte bundle. Companion prototype: 3 async operations, 8 failure leaves, strict JSON envelopes with pinned 117-byte get, 132-byte set, and 72-byte response, per-call destination and auth checks, 334 lines, 18360-byte bundle including 11041 shared policy bytes. Both tiers satisfy the workflow; the companion persists server-side with offline, latency, and cross-device property deltas. Catalogue sketch: 3 generic operations with 3 errors, selectable once a second shipped app needs origin-local persistence.
state.constraints: Zero external users, so no compatibility duty. The catalogue stays closed: nothing ships without compiler admission and distribution review, and no vendor-specific operation is ever admitted. Outbound calls obey the destination allowlist with environment-name credentials that never enter logs. Browser views keep root-only append with disposal that poisons handles and drops late callbacks. A second vendor integration must ship with no vendor-specific compiler patch.
state.experiment: X-R01-1 compares three integration tiers per class after the shared-controls library proof: generic catalogue addition, reviewed adapter package, and companion service. Each class ran the same workflow through an injected-host adapter prototype and a typed-boundary companion prototype consuming the shared outbound policy. No browser was launchable, so native-call fidelity rests on cited platform specifications with live verification deferred. Six prototypes total 1638 lines with 54 passing legs; every bundle rebuilds byte-identically.
